main_point.en: Because Jesus has authority over life and death, we can trust Him entirely.
main_point.zh-Hant: 因為耶穌對生命和死亡有權柄，我們可以完全信靠祂。

christ_connection.en: When Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead, He showed that He has power over death. Jesus said, “I am the resurrection and the life” (John 11:25). Because Jesus died on the cross and rose from the dead, we have full assurance that Jesus will one day defeat death forever and resurrect us from the dead.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 耶穌使拉撒路從死裏復活，顯明祂有勝過死亡的能力。耶穌說：「復活在我，生命也在我。」（約翰福音11:25）因為耶穌死在十字架上並從死裏復活，我們可以完全確信，耶穌有一天會永遠勝過死亡，使我們從死裏復活。

content.en:
17 Now when Jesus came, he found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb four days.
18 Bethany was near Jerusalem, about two miles off,
19 and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them concerning their brother.
20 So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary remained seated in the house.
21 Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
22 But even now I know that whatever you ask from God, God will give you.”
23 Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”
24 Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day.”
25 Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live,
26 and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never die. Do you believe this?”
27 She said to him, “Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world.”
28 When she had said this, she went and called her sister Mary, saying in private, “The Teacher is here and is calling for you.”
29 And when she heard it, she rose quickly and went to him.
30 Now Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him.
31 When the Jews who were with her in the house, consoling her, saw Mary rise quickly and go out, they followed her, supposing that she was going to the tomb to weep there.
32 Now when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.”
33 When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, he was deeply moved in his spirit and greatly troubled.
34 And he said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to him, “Lord, come and see.”
35 Jesus wept.
36 So the Jews said, “See how he loved him!”
37 But some of them said, “Could not he who opened the eyes of the blind man also have kept this man from dying?”
content.zh-Hant:
17 耶穌到了，就知道拉撒路在墳墓裏已經四天了。
18 伯大尼離耶路撒冷不遠，約有六里路。
19 有好些猶太人來看馬大和馬利亞，要為她們的兄弟安慰她們。
20 馬大聽見耶穌來了，就出去迎接他；馬利亞卻仍然坐在家裏。
21 馬大對耶穌說：「主啊，你若早在這裏，我兄弟必不死。
22 就是現在，我也知道，你無論向神求甚麼，神也必賜給你。」
23 耶穌說：「你兄弟必然復活。」
24 馬大說：「我知道在末日復活的時候，他必復活。」
25 耶穌對她說：「復活在我，生命也在我。信我的人雖然死了，也必復活；
26 凡活著信我的人必永遠不死。你信這話嗎？」
27 馬大說：「主啊，是的，我信你是基督，是神的兒子，就是那要臨到世界的。」
28 馬大說了這話，就回去暗暗地叫她妹子馬利亞，說：「夫子來了，叫你。」
29 馬利亞聽見了，就急忙起來，到耶穌那裏去。
30 那時，耶穌還沒有進村子，仍在馬大迎接他的地方。
31 那些同馬利亞在家裏安慰她的猶太人，見她急忙起來出去，就跟著她，以為她要往墳墓那裏去哭。
32 馬利亞到了耶穌那裏，看見他，就俯伏在他腳前，說：「主啊，你若早在這裏，我兄弟必不死。」
33 耶穌看見她哭，並看見與她同來的猶太人也哭，就心裏悲歎，又甚憂愁，
34 便說：「你們把他安放在哪裏？」他們回答說：「請主來看。」
35 耶穌哭了。
36 猶太人就說：「你看他愛這人是何等懇切。」
37 其中有人說：「他既然開了瞎子的眼睛，豈不能叫這人不死嗎？」

content.en:
38 Then Jesus, deeply moved again, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
39 Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him, “Lord, by this time there will be an odor, for he has been dead four days.”
40 Jesus said to her, “Did I not tell you that if you believed you would see the glory of God?”
41 So they took away the stone. And Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, “Father, I thank you that you have heard me.
42 I knew that you always hear me, but I said this on account of the people standing around, that they may believe that you sent me.”
43 When he had said these things, he cried out with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out.”
44 The man who had died came out, his hands and feet bound with linen strips, and his face wrapped with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Unbind him, and let him go.”
content.zh-Hant:
38 耶穌又心裏悲歎，來到墳墓前；那墳墓是個洞，有一塊石頭擋著。
39 耶穌說：「你們把石頭挪開。」那死人的姊姊馬大對他說：「主啊，他現在必是臭了，因為他死了已經四天了。」
40 耶穌說：「我不是對你說過，你若信，就必看見神的榮耀嗎？」
41 他們就把石頭挪開。耶穌舉目望天，說：「父啊，我感謝你，因為你已經聽我。
42 我也知道你常聽我，但我說這話是為周圍站著的眾人，叫他們信是你差了我來。」
43 說了這話，就大聲呼叫說：「拉撒路出來！」
44 那死人就出來了，手腳裹著布，臉上包著手巾。耶穌對他們說：「解開，叫他走！」

content.en: Leaders: The Lord of lords entered our suffering to abolish it forever. What hope we have to share!
content.zh-Hant: 領袖：萬主之主進入我們的苦難，為要永遠廢除苦難。我們有何等的盼望可以分享！

content.en: “You need to learn to ask, no matter the situation, ‘How can I glorify God in this?’ Our normal response is to ask, ‘What’s the fastest way out of this situation?’ Christian maturity is learning to look at a situation and knowing that, whatever you face, you face it so God can be glorified through you. Does that make it feel like your life is insignificant and you’re a pawn in God’s global chess game? On the contrary, this passage shows that the glory of God and the love of God are not at odds. Jesus stayed for two reasons: the glory of God (v. 4), and His love for the family (v. 5). God’s glory and His love for you are not enemies. Reject the temptation to pit the two against each other. God’s glory is displayed chiefly in His bottomless love for His people. Was it unloving for Jesus to stay two extra days? If you were Mary and found out Jesus delayed, would it have felt unloving? It would have felt like betrayal. But your feelings are fallible. They are pathological liars. Your feelings say, ‘Jesus doesn’t love you. See? He won’t come. He won’t act.’ Don’t trust your feelings. Let the truth shape your emotions, not your emotions the truth.”¹²
content.zh-Hant: 「無論處境如何，你都需要學習問：『我如何能在這事上榮耀神？』我們通常的反應是問：『最快脫離這處境的方法是甚麼？』基督徒的成熟，是學習看待一個處境，知道無論面對甚麼，你面對它都是為了讓神藉你得榮耀。這是否令你覺得自己的生命微不足道，只是神全球棋局中的一枚棋子？恰恰相反，這段經文顯示神的榮耀和神的愛並不衝突。耶穌留下有兩個原因：神的榮耀（4節）和祂對這家人的愛（5節）。神的榮耀與祂對你的愛並非敵對。要拒絕那使兩者互相對立的試探。神的榮耀主要顯明在祂對子民深不可測的愛中。耶穌多留兩天是否沒有愛心？如果你是馬利亞，發現耶穌延遲了，會不會覺得祂沒有愛心？那會讓人覺得被背叛。但你的感覺會出錯，會不斷向你說謊。你的感覺說：『耶穌不愛你。看見嗎？祂不肯來，也不肯行動。』不要信靠你的感覺。讓真理塑造你的情緒，而不是讓情緒塑造真理。」¹²

content.en: “Death is not a natural extension of life, though many psychologists and thanatologists argue that point today. Death is an enemy, created as a result of sin, and ultimately to be destroyed by God.”¹³
content.zh-Hant: 「死亡不是生命的自然延伸，雖然今天許多心理學家和死亡學者持這種看法。死亡是因罪而產生的仇敵，最終要被神消滅。」¹³

content.en: “Oh, to be more like Jesus. Oh, to willingly enter others’ suffering. The most remarkable part is that Jesus is going to do something that takes their suffering away, but before He fixes their problem, He joins their pain. He enters their grief before He exiles it.”¹⁴
content.zh-Hant: 「願我們更像耶穌，願我們甘心進入別人的苦難。最令人驚奇的是，耶穌將要做一件除去他們苦難的事，但在解決他們的問題之前，祂先與他們一同承受痛苦。祂在驅除他們的悲傷之前，先進入他們的悲傷。」¹⁴

content.en: “It appears to the casual reader that Martha had climbed on board theologically and would no longer have any question about what Jesus could do. Yet a few minutes later she heard Jesus call for the removal of the stone and objected, ‘But, Lord . . . by this time there is a bad odor, for he has been there four days’ (v. 39). So again Martha reminds us of ourselves—a willingness to verbally proclaim biblical truth without applying it in our lives.”¹⁵
content.zh-Hant: 「粗略閱讀的人可能以為馬大在神學上已經接受，對耶穌能做甚麼不再有任何疑問。然而幾分鐘後，她聽見耶穌吩咐挪開石頭，便反對說：『主啊，他現在必是臭了，因為他死了已經四天了。』（39節）因此，馬大再次使我們想起自己：願意口頭宣告聖經真理，卻沒有把它應用在生活中。」¹⁵

content.en: Ancient Near Eastern Jews believed that one’s soul lingered around the body for three days after death. Because Lazarus had been dead four days, his loved ones had lost hope; they believed Jesus was too late. Today’s passage contains a short verse: “Jesus wept” (John 11:35). Scholars debate why Jesus wept, and though the text doesn’t say, we can consider several causes: (1) Jesus wept because He was human and felt sorrow over death, in a general sense and in a personal sense, with the loss of His friend; He felt compassion for Lazarus’s loved ones; (2) Jesus wept over sin’s effects on humanity—both physical and spiritual death; (3) Jesus wept over the people still not understanding His identity and authority. Even after observing Jesus heal diseases and cast out demons, His closest friends didn’t have faith that, though He didn’t arrive within their three-day timeframe of hope, He was capable of restoring life. Jesus had not failed them. For the people to understand His authority, Jesus performed His most astounding miracle: He raised Lazarus from death. Whether or not Jesus wept in grief or over the people’s lack of faith and understanding, one thing is clear: He displayed His power over death.
content.zh-Hant: 古代近東的猶太人相信，人死後靈魂會在身體周圍徘徊三天。拉撒路已死了四天，他的親友因此失去了盼望；他們認為耶穌來得太遲。今天的經文包含一節很短的經文：「耶穌哭了。」（約翰福音11:35）學者對耶穌為何哭泣有不同看法。雖然經文沒有說明，我們可以考慮幾個原因：（1）耶穌哭是因為祂是人，既為死亡這普遍現象悲傷，也因失去朋友而有個人的悲傷；祂憐憫拉撒路的親友；（2）耶穌為罪對人類的影響——身體和屬靈的死亡——而哭；（3）耶穌為人們仍不明白祂的身分和權柄而哭。即使看見耶穌醫病和趕鬼，祂最親近的朋友仍不相信，雖然祂沒有在他們認為有盼望的三天內到達，祂仍有能力使人復活。耶穌沒有辜負他們。為了讓人明白祂的權柄，耶穌行了最驚人的神蹟：祂使拉撒路從死裏復活。無論耶穌是因悲傷，還是因人們缺乏信心和理解而哭，有一件事是清楚的：祂顯明了祂勝過死亡的能力。

content.en: Both the Old and New Testaments teach that one day believers will experience a resurrection of the body from the dead (Isa. 26:19; Ezek. 37:12-14; John 11). The promise of the resurrection is found in the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, and it will take place at His return in the future. Because Jesus was the firstfruits of the resurrection, Christians can be assured that their resurrection will be both bodily and glorious (Phil. 3:20-21; Rom. 8:22-23). The hope of the future resurrection gives Christians confidence that death has been defeated in Jesus’s death and resurrection.
content.zh-Hant: 舊約和新約都教導，信徒有一天會經歷身體從死裏復活（以賽亞書26:19；以西結書37:12-14；約翰福音11章）。復活的應許建立在耶穌從死裏復活之上，並將在祂將來再來時實現。因為耶穌是復活初熟的果子，基督徒可以確信他們將來的復活既是身體的，也是榮耀的（腓立比書3:20-21；羅馬書8:22-23）。將來復活的盼望給基督徒信心，知道死亡已在耶穌的死和復活中被擊敗。

content.en: Lord, because You have all authority, we have hope in death. We may experience sorrow and grief now, but because of Your death on the cross and Your resurrection from the grave, we trust that death has been defeated forever.
content.zh-Hant: 主啊，因為祢擁有一切權柄，我們面對死亡時有盼望。我們現在可能經歷憂傷和悲痛，但因祢死在十字架上並從墳墓復活，我們相信死亡已永遠被擊敗。

question.en: How well do you handle plans changing or falling through (1=Hate it; 10=Roll with it)?
question.zh-Hant: 當計劃改變或落空時，你應對得如何（1分＝非常討厭；10分＝順其自然）？

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You’ll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:
instructions.zh-Hant:
這些可選活動旨在幫助學生互動。你會看到一項討論活動和一項文化連結，後者涉及當今青少年文化中的相關話題。每個小組都不同，請按小組的需要調整活動。目的是讓學生透過與話題和彼此連結，更投入這課內容。

提出以下問題，給學生時間分享答案：

question.en: What kind of problem solver are you: Do you act quickly or do you need more time to think?
question.zh-Hant: 你是哪一種解決問題的人：迅速行動，還是需要更多時間思考？

question.en: What is your typical response when something doesn’t go as planned?
question.zh-Hant: 事情沒有按計劃發生時，你通常如何反應？

question.en: Do you normally believe things will work out or do you tend to brace for disappointment?
question.zh-Hant: 你通常相信事情會有好結果，還是傾向先做好失望的準備？

content.en: We all deal with and handle problems differently. Maybe you like to fix issues as soon as you see a problem; maybe you need time to process your answer before you actually answer. Life can serve us a lot of unexpected situations, but we can trust the Lord’s purpose when our plans fail.
content.zh-Hant: 我們處理和應對問題的方式都不同。也許你喜歡一看見問題就解決；也許你需要時間思考，才會作出回應。生活可能帶來許多意料之外的處境，但當我們的計劃落空，可以信靠主的旨意。

cultural_connection.en: Our world moves quickly. We order fast food and within minutes, the meal is ready. We live fast-paced lives. How has this affected us? Well, many of us aren’t good at waiting. Moving slowly or patiently isn’t our preference. But our desire for instant gratification harms us when it comes to our relationship with God. We wrestle with praying to and trusting in a God who may not give us what we ask for immediately—or at all. We especially struggle when God’s answer results in discomfort, pain, loss, or disappointment. We may question if God is good and if He can be trusted. But we must remember that God is eternal in His nature and understanding. When His timing or His answer doesn’t meet our expectations, we can actually breathe a sigh of relief. Why? Because God sees what we don’t see and knows what we don’t know. More importantly, God does what is good because He is good (Ps. 119:68). When our circumstances don’t feel good in the moment, we can know that our good God will do only what is good and what brings Him glory.
cultural_connection.zh-Hant: 我們的世界運轉迅速。我們點快餐，幾分鐘內餐點就準備好了。我們過著快節奏的生活。這對我們有甚麼影響？我們許多人不擅長等候，不喜歡放慢或耐心等待。但當涉及與神的關係，我們渴望即時滿足的心會傷害我們。我們難以向神禱告並信靠祂，因為祂可能不會立刻賜下我們所求的，甚至可能不賜下。當神的回答帶來不適、痛苦、失去或失望時，我們尤其掙扎。我們可能懷疑神是否良善、是否值得信靠。但我們必須記得，神的本性和理解是永恆的。當祂的時間或回答不符合我們的期望，我們其實可以鬆一口氣。為甚麼？因為神看見我們看不見的，知道我們不知道的。更重要的是，神行善，因為祂是良善的（詩篇119:68）。當我們的處境此刻感覺不好，我們可以知道，良善的神只會做美善和使祂得榮耀的事。

question.en: How did Mary and Martha react to Jesus’s delay? How did they feel?
question.zh-Hant: 馬利亞和馬大如何回應耶穌的延遲？她們有甚麼感受？

answer.en: Leaders: Share Context about Ancient Near Eastern beliefs. Martha’s response included one significant phrase: ‘even now.’ She felt death’s sting, though she knew Jesus, as God’s Son, was able to do all things—despite what she saw and felt. Mary responded without an ‘even now.’ Sure, she may have believed like Martha. But maybe Mary struggled in this moment with why—why Jesus let her brother die, why He came too late. Jesus didn’t scold her; He was moved by her pain. Some of us more easily lean on God’s sovereignty when what we see or feel doesn’t make sense. Some of us feel overwhelmed with sorrow, anger, and doubt. But we can know that even now Jesus sees and cares, and He came to defeat death forever.
answer.zh-Hant: 領袖：分享古代近東信仰的背景。馬大的回答包含一句重要的話：「就是現在」。雖然她感受到死亡的痛苦，卻知道耶穌作為神的兒子，能做一切的事，不受她所見所感的限制。馬利亞的回應沒有「就是現在」。當然，她可能像馬大一樣相信。但也許馬利亞此刻正為何以如此而掙扎：耶穌為甚麼讓她的兄弟死去，為甚麼祂來得太遲？耶穌沒有責備她；祂被她的痛苦感動。我們有些人在所見所感令人不解時，更容易倚靠神的主權；有些人則被悲傷、憤怒和懷疑淹沒。但我們可以知道，就是現在，耶穌也看見並關心我們，祂來是要永遠勝過死亡。

question.en: Why do you think Jesus wept (v. 35)?
question.zh-Hant: 你認為耶穌為甚麼哭了（35節）？

answer.en: Jesus is fully God; He intended to raise Lazarus from death, yet He wept. Jesus wept because, as God the Son, He hurt over sin’s effects on His creation. He wept over His friends’ lack of faith. Jesus wept because He was also fully human. Like us, Jesus experienced the sorrow of death and wept because the people He loved felt the effects of sin—the effects of the fall. He wept because they still didn’t understand who He was and why He came. The Lord of creation wept because He cares deeply for His creation, for human pain and suffering, though He knows believers’ stories end in victorious resurrection.
answer.zh-Hant: 耶穌是完全的神；祂定意使拉撒路從死裏復活，卻仍然哭了。耶穌哭，是因為作為神子，祂為罪對祂受造物的影響感到痛苦。祂為朋友缺乏信心而哭。耶穌哭，也因為祂是完全的人。像我們一樣，耶穌經歷死亡帶來的悲傷；祂哭，是因為祂所愛的人感受到罪的影響——墮落的影響。祂哭，是因為他們仍不明白祂是誰、為甚麼來。創造萬物的主哭了，因為祂深深關心祂所創造的，關心人的痛苦和苦難，雖然祂知道信徒的故事會以得勝的復活結束。

question.en: Read verse 37. When have you wrestled with thoughts like these—that God could’ve prevented suffering but didn’t? Why doesn’t He?
question.zh-Hant: 閱讀37節。你甚麼時候曾為這類想法掙扎：神本可以防止苦難，卻沒有這樣做？祂為甚麼不這樣做？

answer.en: People at Lazarus’s home questioned Jesus: If Jesus was really God, then why didn’t He save Lazarus? Why didn’t He prevent his death? They saw Jesus perform miracles, so their expectations clashed with disappointment when Jesus didn’t do what they expected Him to do. When we suffer or when someone we love suffers or passes away, we wrestle with why God doesn’t answer our prayers or prevent our suffering—especially the suffering of good people who love Him. God invites us to bring these questions to Him. We can keep a few truths in mind: (1) God created a good world, but we are only ‘good’ because of Jesus. We’re all guilty of sin (Rom. 3:10) and actually deserve death—the wages for sin (Rom. 6:23); (2) God often reveals more of Himself to us in suffering, as He does in this passage (see also Job 42:5). Suffering reminds us of what sin has broken and points us to our deep need for a Savior, for One to give us hope. We suffer because humanity chose rebellion (Gen. 3:6-7). But God redeems our suffering, never wasting it and using it to mold us, to show us He is near, and to reveal the futility of choosing sin. Jesus stepped into our suffering, sacrificing His body in exchange for our eternal peace.
answer.zh-Hant: 拉撒路家中的人質問耶穌：如果耶穌真是神，祂為甚麼沒有救拉撒路？為甚麼沒有阻止他的死？他們看過耶穌行神蹟，因此當耶穌沒有按他們預期的行事，他們的期望便與失望衝突。當我們受苦，或所愛的人受苦、離世，我們會掙扎於神為甚麼不回應禱告或防止苦難，尤其是愛祂的好人所受的苦。神邀請我們把這些問題帶到祂面前。我們可以記住幾個真理：（1）神創造了美好的世界，但我們只有因耶穌才算「好」。我們都有罪（羅馬書3:10），其實都應得死亡——罪的工價（羅馬書6:23）；（2）神常在苦難中向我們更多啟示自己，正如祂在這段經文中所做的（另見約伯記42:5）。苦難提醒我們罪所破壞的事，也指出我們深切需要一位救主，一位賜我們盼望的主。我們受苦，是因為人類選擇悖逆（創世記3:6-7）。但神救贖我們的苦難，從不浪費它，並使用它塑造我們，向我們顯明祂的親近，以及選擇罪的徒然。耶穌進入我們的苦難，犧牲祂的身體，換取我們永恆的平安。

question.en: What does Martha’s comment about the odor reveal about her thoughts (v. 39)?
question.zh-Hant: 馬大提到臭味，顯明她有甚麼想法（39節）？

answer.en: Martha had expressed belief that the Father would give Jesus whatever He asked (v. 22). She had incredible faith, but faith and reality sometimes oppose one another. Martha believed in and trusted Jesus, but at the tomb, she smelled the stench of death; experience told her that they were too late to help Lazarus. Human logic opposes faith and trust in the eternal God. If Martha struggled though Jesus stood right in front of her, then we can expect our human understanding to oppose faith in the Lord at times as well.
answer.zh-Hant: 馬大曾表達信心，相信父會把耶穌所求的一切賜給祂（22節）。她有極大的信心，但信心和現實有時互相對立。馬大相信並信靠耶穌，但在墳墓前，她聞到死亡的臭味；經驗告訴她，幫助拉撒路已經太遲。人的邏輯與對永恆神的信心和信靠相對立。如果耶穌就站在馬大面前，她仍然掙扎，我們也可以預期，人的理解有時會與對主的信心相對立。

question.en: What does Jesus calling Lazarus out of the tomb reveal about His authority over death?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌呼叫拉撒路走出墳墓，顯明祂對死亡有甚麼權柄？

answer.en: Jesus calling out Lazarus proclaimed He has complete authority over death. When Jesus called out Lazarus, He didn’t ask that He come out. He didn’t hope for Lazarus to come out. He commanded Lazarus to come out, and Lazarus did so immediately. Jesus, the Creator of life, has control of life, even after death. This passage proves that Jesus is fully God because only God has control over life and death. If Jesus has all authority over death, then this means death has lost its sting. How much more should we rejoice in this reality!
answer.zh-Hant: 耶穌呼叫拉撒路出來，宣告祂對死亡有完全的權柄。耶穌呼叫拉撒路時，不是請求他出來，也不是盼望他出來；祂命令拉撒路出來，拉撒路就立刻出來了。耶穌是生命的創造者，掌管生命，即使人死後也是如此。這段經文證明耶穌是完全的神，因為只有神掌管生死。如果耶穌對死亡有完全的權柄，這就意味著死亡已失去它的毒鉤。我們更應為這現實喜樂！

question.en: How should believing Jesus defeated death change the way we live now?
question.zh-Hant: 相信耶穌已勝過死亡，應如何改變我們現在的生活方式？

answer.en: When we say that death has lost its sting, we mean that death has no power, no authority, no effect! Death lost its sting because Jesus defeated it when He rose from the grave. Shouldn’t believers look at and respond to death differently than the rest of the world? While unbelievers may fear death, we live in victory! We have hope because of Jesus; we get security because of Jesus; we can live without fear because of Jesus. While we shouldn’t live recklessly but wisely, and the deaths of our loved ones will cause us pain—remember, even Jesus wept over death—we know death isn’t final. Instead, death is a doorway to eternal life and rest for those who believe. We have confidence that Jesus has already won the battle over the grave, and this hope doesn’t waver. We can live life to the fullest, completely devoted to Jesus, because we have assurance. We can handle disappointment here, knowing it isn’t final.
answer.zh-Hant: 當我們說死亡已失去毒鉤，意思是死亡沒有能力、沒有權柄、沒有影響！死亡失去毒鉤，因為耶穌從墳墓復活時勝過了死亡。信徒不是應該以不同於世人的方式看待和回應死亡嗎？不信的人可能害怕死亡，我們卻活在勝利中！因為耶穌，我們有盼望、有安全感，也可以不懼怕地生活。我們不應魯莽，而應明智地生活；所愛之人的死也會令我們痛苦——記得，耶穌也為死亡哭泣——但我們知道死亡不是終點。相反，對信的人來說，死亡是通往永生和安息的門。我們確信耶穌已戰勝墳墓，這盼望不會動搖。因為我們有確據，可以充實地生活，全心委身耶穌。我們能面對今生的失望，因為知道它不是終點。

question.en: How would your life look different if you leaned on faith instead of human logic? How does this passage strengthen your faith?
question.zh-Hant: 如果你依靠信心而非人的邏輯，生活會有甚麼不同？這段經文如何堅固你的信心？

answer.en: Most of us say that we believe Jesus has all authority, but the real question is: Do we live like it? If so, our lives will look completely different from those without hope when we face pain, suffering, disappointment, and death. If we believe Jesus has all authority, we'll choose to trust Him instead of trying to control our circumstances when life feels uncertain. When situations don’t go our way, we'll trust that Jesus still has good purpose instead of panicking. If we believe Jesus has all authority, we'll obey Him, even when it feels uncomfortable or is unpopular. We'll follow Jesus even when it costs us something—even when it costs everything. If we believe Jesus has all authority, we'll forgive others, even when they’re undeserving. When we really believe Jesus has all authority, we’ll surrender our lives into His hands—our fears, our future, even our death—because it’s the safest place.
answer.zh-Hant: 我們大多數人說自己相信耶穌擁有一切權柄，但真正的問題是：我們是否照著這信念生活？如果是，當我們面對痛苦、苦難、失望和死亡時，我們的生命會與沒有盼望的人完全不同。如果我們相信耶穌擁有一切權柄，當生活感覺不確定時，我們會選擇信靠祂，而不是試圖掌控環境。當事情不如所願，我們不會驚慌，而會相信耶穌仍有美善的目的。如果我們相信耶穌擁有一切權柄，即使感覺不舒服或不受歡迎，我們仍會順服祂；即使要付出代價，甚至付出一切，我們仍會跟隨祂。如果我們相信耶穌擁有一切權柄，即使別人不配，我們仍會饒恕他們。當我們真正相信耶穌擁有一切權柄，就會把生命交在祂手中——我們的恐懼、未來，甚至死亡——因為那是最安全的地方。

content.en: If God delivers His children from “all of their troubles,” then why do we still experience pain? “All their troubles” does not mean a life free from suffering; it points to the faithful compassion of God, His steadfast presence, and the ultimate rescue of His children that will take place when He comes back. The Lord doesn’t ignore pain. He is a God who listens. He hears every cry and sees every hardship. He promises that rescue will come, but it does not always look the way we think it should. Deliverance can take place in many different ways: strength to persevere through a trial, comfort in the midst of pain, or ultimate restoration found in eternity with Christ. While we cannot expect to see total deliverance from all our troubles here on earth, we can expect to be held and seen by a loving God until we experience that ultimate deliverance. We see a clear picture of the nearness of God and heartache coexisting in John 11. When Jesus arrived after the death of His friend, Lazarus, we see that Mary and Martha are grieving deeply. Both Mary and Martha suggested that if Jesus had made it to them faster, Lazarus would still be alive. Jesus knew what was coming next. He knew that He had the power to raise Lazarus from the dead, but His knowledge of the future did not stop Him from entering into Mary and Martha’s sorrow and being “deeply moved” by it. This should remind us of the beautiful truth that God is not distant while we are hurting; He intentionally draws near and enters our sorrow. Just like Mary and Martha, we don’t always understand or agree with God’s timeframe, nor do we see the whole picture, but we can trust in His promises. While God’s Word doesn’t guarantee that His love will come in the form of instant solutions, we are promised that His love will show up in the form of His presence, no matter the circumstance.
content.zh-Hant: 如果神救祂的兒女脫離「一切患難」，為甚麼我們仍然經歷痛苦？「一切患難」並不意味著生活沒有苦難；它指向神信實的憐憫、祂堅定的同在，以及祂再來時對兒女最終的拯救。主不忽視痛苦。祂是聆聽的神，聽見每一聲呼求，看見每一個艱難。祂應許拯救必會來臨，但不一定以我們認為應有的方式出現。拯救可以用許多不同方式發生：有力量在試煉中堅持、在痛苦中得到安慰，或在與基督同在的永恆中得到最終的恢復。雖然我們不能期望在地上完全脫離一切患難，但可以期待慈愛的神擁抱並看顧我們，直到經歷最終的拯救。在約翰福音11章，我們清楚看見神的親近與心痛同時存在。耶穌在朋友拉撒路死後到達時，我們看見馬利亞和馬大深深悲傷。她們都表示，如果耶穌早些來，拉撒路就不會死。耶穌知道接下來會發生甚麼，知道自己有能力使拉撒路從死裏復活；但祂對未來的知識沒有阻止祂進入馬利亞和馬大的悲傷，並因此「心裏悲歎」。這應提醒我們一個美好的真理：我們受傷時，神並不遙遠；祂刻意走近，進入我們的悲傷。正如馬利亞和馬大，我們不總是明白或認同神的時間，也看不見全貌，但我們可以信靠祂的應許。神的話沒有保證祂的愛會以即時解決問題的方式出現，卻應許無論處境如何，祂的愛會以祂同在的方式顯明。

question.en: Have you ever felt like God was distant from you while you were hurting? What made you feel that way?
question.zh-Hant: 你受傷時是否曾覺得神離你很遠？甚麼令你有這種感覺？

question.en: How does knowing that God promises to be present at all times change the way you view suffering?
question.zh-Hant: 知道神應許時刻與你同在，如何改變你看待苦難的方式？

prayer.en: Heavenly Father, thank You for not always answering my prayers in the way I think You should. Your ways and Your thoughts are far higher than mine, and I trust that Your plans for me are good even when I can’t see the good in my circumstance.
prayer.zh-Hant: 天父，感謝祢沒有總是按我認為應有的方式回應禱告。祢的道路和意念遠高過我的；即使我看不見處境中的益處，我仍相信祢對我的計劃是美善的。

content.en: We’re often surprised when our expectations are wrong. Jews had expectations for the Messiah, and Jesus was not the Messiah the people expected. Instead of coming in power with prestige and popularity, He was rejected. Jesus was no stranger to suffering and pain. He was not hidden from hardship; He entered fully into a broken world and took on the total penalty of sin. When we are hurting, it is easy to feel like God is far off and doesn’t understand what we are going through, but that couldn’t be further from the truth. Isaiah 53 shows us that Jesus not only understands our feelings, but He experienced them. He is familiar with the pain of being misunderstood, mocked, dismissed, and rejected. Not only did He feel emotional pain, but He experienced spiritual and physical anguish as well. We don’t serve a distant and blind God. We commune personally with a Savior who walked through deep suffering. In the main passage from this week, we see a connection to Isaiah 53. The Son of God chose to bear the weight of emotional pain alongside those He loved who were grieving. Seeing Jesus weep in John 11 and described as the Suffering Servant in the book of Isaiah helps us to realize His empathy for us. When we feel that we don’t belong and our pain doesn’t matter, we can rest in the fact that Jesus understands and sees us. Because we serve a risen Savior who knows our pain, we can bring every hurt to Jesus and trust that we will be met with compassion and with the promise that our suffering will not have the final word.
content.zh-Hant: 當我們的期望落空，常常感到驚訝。猶太人對彌賽亞有期望，而耶穌並不是他們所期待的彌賽亞。祂沒有帶著權勢、聲望和人氣而來，反而被人拒絕。耶穌對苦難和痛苦並不陌生。祂沒有被隔絕於艱難之外，而是完全進入破碎的世界，承擔了罪全部的刑罰。當我們受傷時，很容易覺得神遠離我們，不明白我們的經歷，但事實絕非如此。以賽亞書53章讓我們看見，耶穌不只明白我們的感受，祂也親身經歷過。祂熟悉被誤解、嘲笑、輕視和拒絕的痛苦。祂不僅感受過情緒上的痛苦，也經歷過靈裏和身體上的痛楚。我們所事奉的神並不遙遠，也不會對我們的苦況視而不見。我們與一位經歷深重苦難的救主有親密的交通。在本週主要經文中，我們看見與以賽亞書53章的連結。神的兒子選擇與祂所愛、正在悲傷的人一同承擔情感痛苦的重擔。在約翰福音11章看見耶穌哭泣，並在以賽亞書看見祂被描述為受苦的僕人，幫助我們認識祂對我們的體恤。當我們覺得自己沒有歸屬、痛苦無關緊要時，可以安息於耶穌明白並看見我們這事實。因為我們事奉一位知道我們痛苦、已經復活的救主，我們可以把每一個傷痛帶到耶穌面前，相信祂會以憐憫待我們，並應許苦難不會是最終的結局。

question.en: What effect does this description of Jesus have on you?
question.zh-Hant: 這段對耶穌的描述對你有甚麼影響？

question.en: Instead of coming as the powerful King Israel expected, Jesus was born as a baby and experienced all types of suffering while here. Why is the truth that Jesus was not shielded from suffering comforting?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌沒有以以色列所期待的大能君王身分而來，而是生為嬰孩，在世上經歷各樣苦難。知道耶穌沒有被保護得不受苦，為甚麼令人安慰？

prayer.en: Jesus, thank You for experiencing all types of suffering, even death on a cross, so that we could have a Savior who understands us. Help me to remember Your empathy so that I can run to You more quickly in trials.
prayer.zh-Hant: 耶穌，感謝祢經歷各樣苦難，甚至死在十字架上，使我們能有一位明白我們的救主。求祢幫助我記得祢的體恤，使我在試煉中更快奔向祢。

content.en: This passage shifts the focus from Jesus understanding what we walk through to Him carrying what belonged to us. Jesus didn’t come only to walk with those who were suffering, but He stepped into our brokenness and took our suffering upon Himself. Isaiah points out that Jesus’s suffering was not punishment for His own mistakes but ours. This truth has the power to set us free. We don’t have to carry the weight that Jesus died to release us from. Mistakes we wish we could unmake, the pressure to perform perfectly, guilt over wrong choices, shame from hidden darkness in our lives—Jesus took the weight of all this and more on Himself and carried it to the cross. Isaiah prophesied: ‘He was pierced for our transgressions; he was crushed for our iniquities.’ The punishment that we deserved fell on Jesus, not by accident, but because He willingly accepted it in obedience to the Father. Jesus was completely innocent, yet He willingly took on the pain and consequences He didn’t deserve because of His great love for us. Unlike many of the people who witnessed Jesus’s crucifixion, we know that His suffering wasn’t meaningless or random. His suffering was God’s plan, making His desire for restoration possible and available to all people. Jesus died in our place and made a way for us to have freedom from the weight we were never designed to carry alone. Because of this, we must stop trying to pick back up and carry what He already left in the grave. Jesus not only understood our pain; He took it upon Himself so we could walk in the freedom He won for us instead of the condemnation we deserved.
content.zh-Hant: 這段經文把焦點從耶穌明白我們的經歷，轉向祂承擔原本屬於我們的重擔。耶穌來不只是與受苦的人同行，祂更進入我們的破碎，親自承擔我們的苦難。以賽亞指出，耶穌受苦不是因自己的過錯受罰，而是因我們的過錯。這真理有能力使我們得自由。我們不必背負耶穌捨命要使我們脫離的重擔。我們希望能挽回的錯誤、要求自己表現完美的壓力、錯誤選擇帶來的罪疚、生命中隱藏黑暗帶來的羞恥——耶穌把這一切和更多的重擔擔在自己身上，帶到十字架。以賽亞預言：「他為我們的過犯受害，為我們的罪孽壓傷。」我們應得的刑罰落在耶穌身上，這不是意外，而是因祂順服天父，甘心接受。耶穌完全無辜，卻因對我們的大愛，甘願承擔祂不應得的痛苦和後果。與許多目睹耶穌被釘十字架的人不同，我們知道祂的受苦不是毫無意義或偶然的。祂的受苦是神的計劃，使祂所渴望的復和得以實現，並讓所有人都有機會經歷。耶穌代替我們受死，為我們開路，使我們能從本不該獨自承擔的重擔中得自由。因此，我們必須停止試圖重新拾起、背負祂已留在墳墓裏的重擔。耶穌不僅明白我們的痛苦，也親自承擔，使我們能活在祂為我們贏得的自由中，而不是活在我們應得的定罪中。

question.en: What weight are you carrying even though Jesus took it on Himself?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌已親自承擔甚麼重擔，你卻仍在背負？

question.en: How should the truth that Jesus did not earn the punishment He received, but He took the penalty we deserved, change the way we live?
question.zh-Hant: 耶穌所受的刑罰並非祂應得，而是祂承擔了我們應得的刑罰；這真理應如何改變我們的生活？

prayer.en: Jesus, thank You for taking the punishment I deserved and the weight of guilt and shame on Yourself. Help me to live in the freedom You won for me.
prayer.zh-Hant: 耶穌，感謝祢親自承擔我應得的刑罰，以及罪疚和羞恥的重擔。求祢幫助我活在祢為我贏得的自由中。

content.en:
Have you ever been deceived by how something looked? Maybe the way it appeared was drastically different in person than you expected. Appearances can be deceiving, and Jesus’s death certainly appeared like loss. Isaiah 53 reminds us that Jesus’s suffering did not end in defeat but in victory. This passage shows us that even in death, God was working out the greatest redemption story to ever be written. The perfect Son of God gave His life as a final sacrifice for sin. Although He had done no wrong, ‘it was the will of the LORD to crush him’ so that many would be brought into right standing with God. Just like the death of Lazarus wasn’t final, Jesus rose from the grave, claiming victory over death and changing the end of the story for those who would put their trust in Him. Because of the victory of Christ, suffering no longer has the final word, and sin and death no longer have power to define the ending of our story.

Let’s think back to Mary and Martha. While they had heard of the ending of the story, they had no idea what the next chapter held for them and for their brother, for whom they were grieving. As far as they knew, their brother’s death was final, and all hope was lost. They were confused and hurt that Jesus had not gotten there in time to heal him. In the same way, we may walk through times when life feels confusing, unfair, lonely, and disappointing, but because Jesus bore our sin and conquered the grave, we know that life exists even in situations that seem like loss. This prophecy written in Isaiah and fulfilled in the Gospels reminds us that God is always moving in ways that we cannot see and may not understand, but we can walk with hope knowing that He has already won the ultimate victory for us.
content.zh-Hant:
你是否曾被事物的外表欺騙？也許實際看到的樣子與你的期望大不相同。外表可能具有欺騙性，耶穌的死看起來確實像是失敗。以賽亞書53章提醒我們，耶穌的苦難不是以失敗結束，而是以勝利結束。這段經文讓我們看見，即使在死亡中，神仍在成就有史以來最偉大的救贖故事。完全的神子獻出生命，作為罪的最終祭物。雖然祂沒有做錯，「耶和華卻定意將他壓傷」，使許多人得以與神和好。正如拉撒路的死不是終點，耶穌也從墳墓復活，勝過死亡，改變了信靠祂之人的故事結局。因著基督的勝利，苦難不再是最終的結局，罪和死亡也不再有權力決定我們故事的結局。

讓我們回想馬利亞和馬大。雖然她們曾聽聞故事的結局，卻不知道下一章對她們和她們所哀悼的兄弟意味著甚麼。就她們所知，兄弟的死是終局，一切盼望都失去了。耶穌沒有及時到達醫治他，使她們困惑和受傷。同樣，我們可能經歷生活令人困惑、不公平、孤獨和失望的時刻；但因為耶穌擔當了我們的罪，勝過墳墓，我們知道即使在看似失敗的處境中也有生命。以賽亞所寫、在福音書中實現的預言提醒我們，神一直以我們看不見、可能也不明白的方式工作；但我們可以帶著盼望前行，因為知道祂已為我們贏得最終的勝利。

question.en: Why does Jesus’s death and resurrection give us the ability to walk with hope, even when we suffer?
question.zh-Hant: 為甚麼耶穌的死和復活使我們即使受苦，仍能帶著盼望前行？

question.en: God is faithful to keep His Word. How does reflecting on the fulfilled prophecies of the Old Testament encourage you in difficult times?
question.zh-Hant: 神信實地持守祂的話。思想舊約中已應驗的預言，如何在困難時鼓勵你？

prayer.en: Lord, thank You for being a God who is always working behind the scenes to bring about Your plans and purposes. Help me to take joy in remembering that because of who You are, suffering isn’t final.
prayer.zh-Hant: 主啊，感謝祢一直在幕後工作，成就祢的計劃和旨意。求祢幫助我因記得祢是誰而喜樂，知道苦難不是終點。

content.en: When Jesus was told that His friend, Lazarus, had become sick, He said something that would have shocked anyone who heard it: Lazarus’s illness was for the “glory of God.” Jesus then intentionally waited two days before traveling to see Lazarus and his sisters, and during this timeframe, Lazarus died. To those who were mourning, this death felt confusing, unnecessary, and painful. Jesus deeply loved Lazarus, yet He allowed his death to happen in order that God’s glory was revealed, even through pain. God’s glory through our pain is something that can be hard to see and understand when our own pain often feels pointless. While walking through loss, disappointment, mental health struggles, or family issues, we understandably question why God would allow us to hurt. Jesus, when He wept over Lazarus’s death, shows us that while we shouldn’t deny the existence of pain, we should remember that pain and death do not have the final word. Romans 8:28 reminds us that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him. This “good” should not be misinterpreted as the absence of pain because, as believers, Jesus promised we will have trouble in this world (John 16:33). Instead, we should remember that this “good” represents God’s greater purpose of making us more like His Son, which He can accomplish through working all things together. His plans are good, and they cannot be stopped. In the story of Lazarus’s death, the “good” accomplished was God’s glory revealed and lives changed through belief in Jesus. God is not the author of pain, but like we see in this passage, He does use it to draw people to faith. Even when we don’t understand why difficult things happen, we can be confident that God is present in our pain with us and that our suffering isn’t the end.
content.zh-Hant: 耶穌聽說祂的朋友拉撒路病了，便說了一句讓聽見的人都會震驚的話：拉撒路的病是為「神的榮耀」。耶穌接著刻意等了兩天，才動身去見拉撒路和他的姊妹；在這段時間裏，拉撒路死了。對哀悼的人而言，這死亡令人困惑，似乎沒有必要，並且帶來痛苦。耶穌深愛拉撒路，卻容許他死去，為要使神的榮耀即使透過痛苦也能顯明。我們自己的痛苦常感覺毫無意義，因此很難看見和理解神如何透過我們的痛苦得榮耀。當我們經歷失去、失望、心理健康的掙扎或家庭問題，很自然會問神為甚麼容許我們受傷。耶穌為拉撒路的死哭泣，向我們顯明，雖然我們不應否認痛苦的存在，卻應記得痛苦和死亡不是最終結局。羅馬書8:28提醒我們，神使萬事互相效力，叫愛祂的人得益處。這「益處」不應被誤解為沒有痛苦，因為耶穌應許信徒在世上會有苦難（約翰福音16:33）。相反，我們應記得，這「益處」代表神使我們更像祂兒子的更大旨意；祂能藉著使萬事互相效力成就這旨意。祂的計劃是美善的，無法被阻止。在拉撒路死亡的故事中，所成就的「益處」是神的榮耀得以顯明，人的生命因相信耶穌而改變。神不是痛苦的製造者，但正如我們在這段經文中看見，祂確實使用痛苦引領人相信。即使我們不明白困難為甚麼發生，也可以確信神在痛苦中與我們同在，而苦難不是終點。

question.en: Many people believed in Jesus as a result of Lazarus’s death. How does this challenge you to reframe your thoughts about your own trials?
question.zh-Hant: 許多人因拉撒路的死而相信耶穌。這如何挑戰你重新看待自己的試煉？

question.en: Knowing that the “good” in Romans 8:28 refers to God’s will, how can the truth that He works all things together for good encourage you?
question.zh-Hant: 知道羅馬書8:28中的「益處」指神的旨意，祂使萬事互相效力帶來益處的真理如何鼓勵你？

prayer.en: Father, thank You for being the only One who is capable of working all things together for good. When I feel like something is too dark to be used for good, remind me that nothing is outside of Your control.
prayer.zh-Hant: 父啊，感謝祢是唯一能使萬事互相效力帶來益處的主。當我覺得某事太黑暗、無法帶來益處時，求祢提醒我，沒有甚麼在祢的掌管之外。
